method: Start with the almost invisible film of liquid water that sits on an icy surface, even when the air is below water's normal freezing point.

ingredients.name: sync keeping current files aligned across devices
backup preserving restorable earlier copies
accidental deletion travelling through sync
separate recovery history

method: Keep the recipe and split the functions: sync updates connected devices so they show the same current files, which is useful for access and collaboration.
Distil backup separately: it keeps recoverable copies or versions from earlier points in time, ideally with retention that is not immediately changed when the live file changes.

Serve the practical consequence: if you delete or corrupt a synced file, that change may spread everywhere; a separate backup can let you restore the version from before the mistake, so sync alone is not a complete backup plan.

ingredients.name: one query parameter value
percent-encoding for spaces and the ampersand
the encoded value red%20tea%20%26%20cake
separation between data and URL syntax

method: Treat everything after `q=` as one value you want the server to receive; a raw ampersand normally separates query parameters, so leaving it unchanged would split the value early.
Percent-encode the spaces as `%20` and the literal ampersand as `%26`, producing `?q=red%20tea%20%26%20cake` for that value.
When the server decodes the query parameter, it receives `red tea & cake`; the encoding protects data characters that would otherwise be mistaken for URL structure.
assistant_response.title: The Query-String Separator
